thread:
maya: Quick follow-up on the quant RFC — canary showed ~3.2% quality drop on some intents in the 4-bit path, specifically long-tail prompts. Want to sync propagation vs calibration strategies.
priya: Ugh. Which layer types are the biggest offenders? attention, feedforward, or embedding scales?
evan: From the logs it looks like early-layer attention projections + residual accumulation. Noise amplifies across residual adds.
sasha: That matches my sim runs — per-layer scale mismatch causes distribution shift that later layers treat as signal.
maya: Right. Two angles: 1) better offline calibration (per-channel per-head) 2) runtime micro-recalibration for hot prompts. Tradeoffs: offline costs + storage vs latency/complexity at runtime. Thoughts?
jules: For offline, we should keep calibration artifacts lightweight. Per-channel int8 histograms + a small scale vector for fp8 bias correction. No full-copies of weights.
priya: Runtime recalibration is appealing for long-tail but tricky. We can sample first N tokens and adapt quant scales, but that adds latency and could bias outputs mid-generation.
evan: Could do a cheap prefix-only calibration pass: run the first 16 tokens through a low-overhead stat collector (no extra compute-heavy ops), adjust KV scale before full decode.
maya: Example quick pseudo: ```python
def prefix_calibrate(model, prefix, sample_k=16):
    stats = collect_activations(model, prefix[:sample_k])
    scales = estimate_scales(stats, per_channel=True)
    model.runtime.set_scales(scales)
    return model
```
priya: Nice. But we need safety: if scale changes > X% we should reject and fall back to a higher-precision path. Otherwise a bad prefix could make things worse.
sasha: Agree. Add a simple degradation score: run both calibrated fast path and a small reference (fp16) batch on the prefix and compute embedding/likelihood delta. If delta > threshold, fallback.
ejobs-bot: Canary deployed: quant-canary-v3 started at 3123456900 on dedicated-qa. Logs: canary_success=87%, canary_quality_drop=3.2%.
maya: Good to know. For thresholds, propose: scale delta > 25% OR embedding cosine delta > 0.05 triggers fallback. We can tune.
jules: Ops concern: storing per-model per-version calibration blobs explodes metadata. Proposal: canonicalize blobs by calibration-hash and reference-count, TTL them after N days.
evan: Also need telemetry fields: calibration_used(bool), calibration_hash, calibration_delta_pct, fallback_reason, prefix_token_count. Send these to traces and cost dashboard.
priya: For evaluation, we should add a 'calibration robustness' axis to our perf/qual matrix: synthetic distribution shifts, prompt length, and prefix noise. Automate with existing eval harness.
sasha: One more: quant noise propagation model — we may be able to statically predict amplification by measuring residual norm growth. If predicted amplification > threshold we force higher precision on the residual path.
maya: That's interesting. Could be a compile-time hint: annotate residual edges with predicted amplification factor and let runtime route to int8/16 accordingly.
jules: Implementation detail: make the precision routing decision an idempotent function of model-version + input-shape + calibration-hash. Helps reproducibility and rollbacks.
priya: Rollout playbook: 1) offline calibration artifacts validated on eval suite, 2) canary with telemetry flags, 3) sampled runtime prefix-calibration on 1% traffic, 4) escalate or rollout. Document error codes for fallback reasons.
emma-bot: Alert: observed 14 fallback events in last hour for canary, top reason: embedding_delta.
evan: We should also measure latency p95 for the prefix_calibrate path. If p95 > 200ms we disable runtime path automatically.
maya: Action items: @priya to draft prefix-calibrate API + safety thresholds, @evan to add telemetry fields and sim for residual amplification, @jules to propose artifact canonicalization + TTL, @sasha to add residual-edge compile hint RFC.
priya: I'll draft the API sketch in the RFC doc today. Will include example cURL and SDK surfaces.
maya: Thanks. If we can get these primitives in next sprint we can try a staged canary. :thumbsup:
evan: FYI I pushed a tiny sim notebook to internal gist: /gists/quant-prop-sim (logs and plots).
sasha: +1 to notebook, will reproduce with a few Llama-family checkpoints.
jules: I'll map out metadata schema for calibration blobs and reference-counting.
maya: Great thread. We'll reconvene after PRs.
